units.source_text: 前太政大臣向葛城山招请法力高明的修道僧，正在等候他们来到，替柏木诵经念咒。

en.t: The former Grand Minister had summoned ascetic monks of great spiritual power from Mount Katsuragi and was waiting for them to arrive and chant sutras and spells for Kashiwagi.

units.source_text: 近来邸内修建法事，念经祈祷，已经非常喧吵。

en.t: Recently the mansion had already become extremely noisy with Buddhist services, sutra chanting, and prayers.

units.source_text: 如今又听人劝告，派遣柏木的诸弟到各处去寻找遁迹深山之中、世间少人闻知的种种圣僧。

en.t: Now, following more advice, he sent Kashiwagi's younger brothers everywhere to search for holy monks who had withdrawn deep into the mountains and were scarcely known in the world.

units.source_text: 于是来了许多形容怪异、面目可憎的山人。

en.t: As a result, many mountain recluses arrived, strange in appearance and unpleasant to look at.

units.source_text: 柏木的病状，并无特别可指的疾痛，只是忧愁苦闷，时时放声哭泣。

en.t: Kashiwagi's illness had no particular pain or symptom that could be named; he was simply sunk in sorrow and anguish, and often cried aloud.

units.source_text: 据阴阳师占卜，都说是有女魂作祟。

en.t: According to the divinations of the yin-yang masters, they all said that a woman's spirit was causing the affliction.

units.source_text: 大臣也信以为然。

en.t: The Minister believed this as well.

units.source_text: 然而做了许多法事，并无鬼怪出现。

en.t: Yet even after many rites were performed, no spirit appeared.

units.source_text: 大臣不胜烦恼，因此又招请了这许多山僧来。

en.t: The Minister was overwhelmed with anxiety, and so he summoned this great number of mountain monks.

units.source_text: 有一个圣僧，身材高大，面目狰狞，厉声诵念陀罗尼咒。

en.t: One holy monk was tall, fierce in face, and chanted dharani spells in a harsh, piercing voice.

units.source_text: 柏木听了，叫道：“哎呀！真讨厌啊！恐是我身罪孽深重之故，听见高声念陀罗尼咒，非常可怕！似觉就要死了。”

en.t: When Kashiwagi heard him, he cried out, "Ah, how hateful! Perhaps because my sins are so heavy, hearing dharani spells chanted so loudly is terrifying. I feel as if I am about to die."

units.source_text: 便蓦地起身，溜出室去，和小侍从谈话。

en.t: He suddenly got up, slipped out of the room, and spoke with Kojiju.

units.source_text: 大臣并不知道，他听侍女们说病人已经睡了，信以为真，便和那个圣僧悄悄地谈话。

en.t: The Minister knew nothing of this; when the serving women told him the patient had fallen asleep, he believed them and quietly spoke with the holy monk.

units.source_text: 这位大臣年纪虽然大了，性情还是愉快活泼，爱说笑话。

en.t: Although this Minister was advanced in years, his temperament was still cheerful and lively, and he liked to make jokes.

units.source_text: 但此时也只得板起面孔对着这山僧，向他叙述柏木起病时情状，以及后来不见任何特征而日重一日的经过。

en.t: But at this moment he could only face the mountain monk with a grave expression and describe how Kashiwagi's illness had begun, and how afterward, with no clear symptoms, it had grown worse day by day.

units.source_text: 他诚恳地请求这山僧使用法力，将这鬼怪发现出来。

en.t: He earnestly begged the mountain monk to use his spiritual power to reveal the possessing spirit.

units.source_text: 由此可见他心中确实十分痛苦。

en.t: From this one could see that his heart was truly in great pain.

units.source_text: 柏木听见了这话，对小侍从说道：“你听我父亲说！他不知道我的病是由于犯了罪恶而起的。阴阳师说有女魂作祟。

en.t: Kashiwagi heard this and said to Kojiju, "Listen to what my father is saying! He does not know that my illness arose because I committed a sin. The yin-yang masters say that a woman's spirit is tormenting me.

units.source_text: 如果真是公主心情执迷，灵魂出窍，附缠在我身上，那么我这卑不足道之人反而不胜荣幸了！

en.t: If it were truly that the Princess's heart was obsessed, her soul had left her body, and it had fastened itself to me, then for someone as low and unworthy as I am, it would be an overwhelming honor.

units.source_text: 我也曾反过来想：心生狂妄之念，身犯弥天大罪，毁坏他人名节，不顾自己前途，在古昔时代并非没有其例。

en.t: I have also thought of it the other way: in ancient times there were indeed examples of men who conceived reckless desires, committed enormous sins, ruined another person's honor, and disregarded their own future.

units.source_text: 然而身列其境，实甚痛苦。

en.t: Yet when one stands in such a position oneself, it is truly unbearable.

units.source_text: 源氏大人已经知道我这罪行，使我没有面目生存于世，这恐怕是由于他的威仪光彩赫赫逼人之故吧。

en.t: Lord Genji already knows of my offense, leaving me without the face to live in this world; perhaps this is because his majesty and radiance press upon me so overwhelmingly.

units.source_text: 其实我并无极恶大罪，然而自从试乐那天傍晚和源氏大人相见之后，立刻心情紊乱，病倒在床，魂灵游离，不复返身了。

en.t: In truth I have committed no utterly wicked crime, yet ever since I met Lord Genji on the evening of the rehearsal, my mind was thrown into disorder, I fell ill in bed, and my soul wandered away and no longer returned to my body.

units.source_text: 如果我的魂灵彷徨在六条院内，务请快结前裾，使它归还我身。”

en.t: If my soul is wandering within the Rokujo estate, please quickly tie the front hem of your robe and make it return to my body."

units.source_text: 说时声音非常微弱，忽泣忽笑，显然是丧失魂灵的躯壳里说出来的。

en.t: As he spoke, his voice was extremely faint; now crying, now laughing, he seemed clearly to be speaking from a body that had lost its soul.

units.source_text: 小侍从告诉柏木：三公主也一向含羞忍耻，忧愁恐惧。

en.t: Kojiju told Kashiwagi that the Third Princess too had long been enduring shame and humiliation, full of sorrow and fear.

units.source_text: 柏木听了这话，眼前依稀恍惚地看见三公主伤心失意、肌黄肤瘦的面影，便确信自己的魂灵已经脱躯而出，驰往公主身边，心中越发痛苦难堪了。

en.t: When Kashiwagi heard this, he dimly seemed to see before his eyes the image of the Third Princess, heartbroken, desolate, pale, and thin, and he became convinced that his own soul had left his body and flown to her side, which made his anguish still harder to bear.

units.source_text: 便对小侍从说：“从今不要再谈公主之事了！我身短命而死，这点怨气恐将成为公主将来入道成佛之羁绊，思之不胜遗憾。

en.t: He then said to Kojiju, "From now on, do not speak of the Princess again. If I die young, I fear this resentment of mine may become an obstacle to the Princess's future renunciation and enlightenment, and the thought fills me with regret.

units.source_text: 公主怀孕已将足月，我只指望听到安产的消息，然后死去。

en.t: The Princess's pregnancy is almost at full term, and I only hope to hear news of her safe delivery before I die.

units.source_text: 那天晚上我梦见小猫，只我一人心知是怀胎之兆，却无人可以告诉，此事我甚感悲伤！”

en.t: That night I dreamed of a kitten, and I alone knew in my heart that it was a sign of pregnancy, but there was no one I could tell; this made me deeply sad."

units.source_text: 柏木百感交集，心情郁结，那愁眉苦脸的模样，可厌可怕，然而又甚可怜。

en.t: Kashiwagi was overcome by countless emotions and his heart was stifled with grief; his sorrowful, tormented appearance was repellent and frightening, yet also deeply pitiable.

units.source_text: 小侍从也忍不住哭起来了。

en.t: Kojiju too could no longer hold back her tears and began to cry.
